item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q002_mazg_hise_remote_homology","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, d1vmga_ (SCCS a.204.1.2) is in the MazG-like family, whereas d1y6xa1 (a.204.1.4) is in the HisE-like (PRA-PH) family. Both families belong to the all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatases superfamily a.204.1 and fold a.204. Thus SCOPe supports probable remote common ancestry at the superfamily level, not close family-level homology or equivalence. The classification does not justify transferring the HisE annotation (phosphoribosyl-ATP pyrophosphatase), substrate specificity, catalytic residues, or pathway role to d1vmga_, whose SCOPe protein entry is a hypothetical Sulfolobus solfataricus protein; nor does it justify assigning MazG-specific activity to d1y6xa1. Either domain may provide a coarse structural template for the conserved domain architecture, but not an automatically reliable active-site, ligand, functional, or whole-protein template, and they are not interchangeable family representatives. Exact function would require independent evidence such as sequence/active-site analysis plus ligand-bound structural or direct biochemical activity data.","evidence_used":["/api/v1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1vmga_","/api/v1/releases/2.08/resolve/d1y6xa1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/113676","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/122676","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/116995","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/140801","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/116994","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/140798","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/116993","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/140797","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/101386","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/101385"]}]}
